# Workflow

The Workflow category has 12 tasks. Each entry shows the task's latest revision, the one the palette adds. See [Reading an entry](./overview#reading-an-entry).

> [!NOTE]
> The palette lists **For each** first in this category. It isn't a catalogue task: it repeats a task once per item of a list. See [For each](../fundamentals/tasks#for-each).

## Acquire Lock

This task attempts to obtain a lock with the specified name. If no other workflow in the team is using a lock with that name, a lock with that name and is created. If another workflow in the team is using a lock with the specified name, the current workflow waits until the lock is available.

- **Slug:** `acquire-lock`
- **Type:** `acquirelock`
- **Revision:** 2
- **Image:** None. Flow runs this task itself.

> [!NOTE]
> Revision 1 says **Timeout** is in seconds and defaults it to 300, but Flow reads it in milliseconds, so the lock expires after 300 milliseconds. Revision 2 says milliseconds and defaults to 300000, which is 5 minutes. Upgrade a node pinned to revision 1 in the editor.

**Parameters**

| Label | Name | Type | Required | Default | Helper text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lock Name | `key` | Text | Yes |  | A value to identify the lock. |
| Timeout | `timeout` | Number | Yes | `300000` | Duration before the lock expires, in milliseconds |

No results.

### Example

Let only one run in the workspace deploy to an environment at a time. A run that reaches the lock while another holds it waits its turn.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Task name** | `lock-env` |
| **Lock Name** | `deploy-$(params.environment)` |
| **Timeout** | `900000`: 15 minutes in milliseconds, longer than the deploy takes |

For a run with `environment` set to `production`, the lock is named `deploy-production`. A run that finds it held shows **Waiting** and tries again every 5 seconds, without using up its timeout. Link the deploy tasks after `lock-env`, then a **Release Lock** task with the same **Lock Name**. The lock is shared by every workflow in the workspace, and is freed when Release Lock runs, when the run ends, or when **Timeout** passes, whichever comes first. The task returns no results.

### Common problems

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A second run gets the lock while the first is still working | **Timeout** passed. It's in milliseconds, although revision 1 says seconds, so `300` there lasts 300 milliseconds. | Set **Timeout** in milliseconds, longer than the locked tasks take. Upgrade a node that's still on revision 1. |
| The task stays **Waiting** | Another run in the workspace holds a lock of that name, from this workflow or any other. | Find the run holding it. The lock is freed when that run releases it or ends, or when its **Timeout** passes. |
| The task fails with `acquirelock requires a key and a timeout.` | **Timeout** has no value, or isn't a number once references resolve, such as a parameter that holds `15m`. | Give **Timeout** in milliseconds, in digits only. |

## Manual Approval

Pauses workflow until approval is actioned. If no approver group is specified then this task can be approved by anyone in the team, and only requires 1 approval.

- **Slug:** `manual-approval`
- **Type:** `approval`
- **Revision:** 2
- **Image:** None. Flow runs this task itself.

> [!NOTE]
> The hint for **Number of Approvals (optional)** says "Only respected if Approver Group is specified", but Flow applies the number whether or not you choose an approver group. Leave it blank when one approval is enough. See [Number of Approvals applies without an approver group](../introduction/known-issues#number-of-approvals-applies-without-an-approver-group).

**Parameters**

| Label | Name | Type | Required | Default | Helper text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Approver Group (optional) | `approverGroupId` | Select | No |  | Limit the approvers to the members in this group |
| Number of Approvals (optional) | `numberOfApprovals` | Number | No |  | Only respected if Approver Group is specified |

**Results**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `approvalStatus` | The status of the approval task, can be approved or rejected. |
| `approvalDate` | Date and time of the action |
| `approvalUserName` | Username of the approver |
| `approvalUserEmail` | Email address of the approver |
| `approvalComments` | Additional comments added by the approver |

### Example

Pause a release for one person's sign-off, then let a later task report who decided. This is the `approve` task in [Pass results between tasks with an approval](../tutorials/pass-results-with-an-approval).

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Task name** | `approve` |
| **Approver Group (optional)** | Blank, so any workspace owner or editor can decide |
| **Number of Approvals (optional)** | Blank, so one decision completes the task |

The task returns:

| Result | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `approvalStatus` | `approved` or `rejected` |
| `approvalDate` | When the approver acted, in ISO 8601 UTC, such as `2026-11-04T05:12:44.120Z` |
| `approvalUserName` | The approver's name |
| `approvalUserEmail` | The approver's email address |
| `approvalComments` | The approver's comment, or empty |

The run waits at `approve`, without using up its timeout, until someone selects **Approve** or **Reject** on **Actions**, on Home or on the run page. Approve ends the task **Succeeded** and Reject ends it **Failed**; both set all five results. A later task reads them as `$(tasks.approve.results.approvalStatus)`. See [Actions](../fundamentals/actions).

### Common problems

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| After **Reject**, the next task shows **Skipped** and the run ends **Failed** | A rejection fails the task, and a success link runs the next task only when the task succeeds. | To carry on either way, use an always link and read `approvalStatus` in the next task. To act only on a rejection, use a failure link. |
| With no approver group, the approval waits for more decisions, such as **0/2 approvals** | Flow applies **Number of Approvals (optional)** with or without a group, although its hint says otherwise. | Leave it blank when one decision is enough. See [Number of Approvals applies without an approver group](../introduction/known-issues#number-of-approvals-applies-without-an-approver-group). |
| Someone sees the approval but can't decide it | Readers can't decide. When the task names an approver group, only its members can, and never a machine token. | Give them the editor role, or add them to the group under **Manage workspace › Approver Groups**. |
| **Approver Group (optional)** is disabled and reads "No approver groups configured for this workspace." | The workspace has no approver groups. | Create one under **Manage workspace › Approver Groups**, then choose it. |

## Manual Task

Pauses workflow until manual task is actioned.

- **Slug:** `manual-task`
- **Type:** `manual`
- **Revision:** 1
- **Image:** None. Flow runs this task itself.

**Parameters**

| Label | Name | Type | Required | Default | Helper text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Instructions | `instructions` | Text Area | Yes |  | Steps for end user to follow to perform manual task. |

No results.

### Example

Ask someone to take a database snapshot by hand before a migration runs.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Task name** | `snapshot` |
| **Instructions** | The steps below, in Markdown |

**Instructions**

```markdown
Take a snapshot of the `orders` database before the migration.

1. Name it `pre-migration-$(params.version)`.
2. Wait until it shows **Available**.
3. Select **Complete Successfully**. If the snapshot fails, select **Complete Unsuccessfully**.
```

The run waits at `snapshot`, without using up its timeout, until an owner or editor opens it under **Actions › Manual Tasks** and selects **Complete Successfully**, which ends the task **Succeeded**, or **Complete Unsuccessfully**, which ends it **Failed**. Flow fills in `$(params.version)` before the instructions are shown. The task returns no results.

### Common problems

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The run stays **Waiting** at the task | Nobody has completed it, and a manual task waits indefinitely. | An owner or editor completes it under **Actions › Manual Tasks**, or with **Action** on the run page. |
| After **Complete Unsuccessfully**, the next task shows **Skipped** and the run ends **Failed** | That choice fails the task, and a success link runs the next task only when the task succeeds. | Add a failure link to a task that handles it, such as a notification. |
| Someone sees the task but can't complete it | Readers can't complete manual tasks. | Give them the editor role in the workspace. |

## Release Lock

This task releases a lock with the specified name.

- **Slug:** `release-lock`
- **Type:** `releaselock`
- **Revision:** 1
- **Image:** None. Flow runs this task itself.

**Parameters**

| Label | Name | Type | Required | Default | Helper text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lock Name | `key` | Text | Yes |  | A value to identify as the lock. |

No results.

### Example

Free the lock that the Acquire Lock task `lock-env` took, as soon as the deploy is done, so the next run can deploy.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Task name** | `unlock-env` |
| **Lock Name** | `deploy-$(params.environment)`, the same as on `lock-env` |

Link `unlock-env` after the last task that needs the lock. It frees the lock only when this run holds it, whichever of the run's tasks took it, and succeeds whether or not it freed anything. If a task before it fails and Release Lock is skipped, the lock is still freed when the run ends. The task returns no results.

### Common problems

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release Lock succeeds, but the next run still waits for the lock | **Lock Name** doesn't match the Acquire Lock's exactly once references resolve, and Release Lock succeeds when it frees nothing. | Give both tasks the same value. Lock names are case-sensitive. |
| The lock stays held while the run waits at a later task, such as an approval | A lock is freed when Release Lock runs or the run ends, not when the locked tasks finish. | Link Release Lock straight after the last task that needs the lock. |

## Run Scheduled Workflow

This task runs the selected workflow one time in the future. It only schedules the workflow, it does not wait for it to execute. Additionally you can pass in workflow parameters if they have been defined.

- **Slug:** `run-scheduled-workflow`
- **Type:** `runscheduledworkflow`
- **Revision:** 1
- **Image:** None. Flow runs this task itself.

**Parameters**

| Label | Name | Type | Required | Default | Helper text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Workflow Reference | `workflowRef` | Text | Yes |  | The reference (or slug) of the Workflow to schedule. |
| Future In | `futureIn` | Number | Yes |  | How many futurePeriod units from now the Workflow should run. |
| Future Period | `futurePeriod` | Text | Yes |  | The unit futureIn is measured in: minutes, hours, days, weeks, or months. |
| Timezone | `timezone` | Text | Yes |  | The timezone time is set in (e.g. America/New_York). Only applied for days, weeks, and months. |
| Time | `time` | Text | Yes |  | The 24-hour clock time (e.g. 14:30) to run at. Only applied for days, weeks, and months. |

No results.

## Run Workflow

This task runs the selected workflow separately. It only triggers the workflow, it does not wait for completion. Additionally you can pass in parameters to the workflow if they have been defined.

- **Slug:** `run-workflow`
- **Type:** `runworkflow`
- **Revision:** 1
- **Image:** None. Flow runs this task itself.

**Parameters**

| Label | Name | Type | Required | Default | Helper text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Workflow Reference | `workflowRef` | Text | Yes |  | The reference (or slug) of the Workflow to run. |
| Wait for the child run to finish | `wait` | Boolean | No | `false` | When enabled, this task waits for the child run and takes its terminal status: the task succeeds only if the child run succeeds. |

No results.

### Example

From a release workflow, start the workflow `deploy-service` for one environment, wait for it, and use the URL it returns.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Task name** | `deploy` |
| **Workflow** | **Deploy service**, chosen from the list. Flow stores its name, `deploy-service`. |
| **Wait for the child run to finish** | On |
| The child's parameters, such as **Environment** | `$(params.environment)` |

The task returns:

| Result | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `workflowRunRef` | The child run's ID |
| `url` | The `url` result the child set with a Set Result Parameter task, once the child succeeds |

Once you choose a workflow, its parameters appear in the form. `deploy` shows **Waiting** until the child run ends, then takes its status, and a later task reads `$(tasks.deploy.results.url)`. With **Wait for the child run to finish** off, the task succeeds as soon as the child starts, with only `workflowRunRef`. See [Child workflows](../fundamentals/runs#child-workflows).

### Common problems

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The task succeeds at once, and a later task gets nothing from the child | **Wait for the child run to finish** is off, the default, so the task returns only `workflowRunRef`. | Turn it on. |
| The task fails with `ChildRunFailed`, and a message such as `Child run <id> ended failed` | With waiting on, the task takes the child's status, and the child didn't succeed. | Select **View Activity** on the task to open the child run and see why. |
| The child fails, or a task in it gets an empty value | The child gets only the values its node passes. The parent run's parameters aren't handed down. | Fill in the child's fields on the node, with references such as `$(params.environment)`. Pass a secret the same way. |
| The task fails with `NestingDepthExceeded` and starts nothing | Runs nest at most 5 deep by default. | Flatten the chain of workflows, or ask an admin to raise **Admin › Settings › Run limits › Maximum Child Workflow Nesting Depth**. |

## Sleep

Sleep for specified duration in milliseconds

- **Slug:** `sleep`
- **Type:** `sleep`
- **Revision:** 1
- **Image:** None. Flow runs this task itself.

**Parameters**

| Label | Name | Type | Required | Default | Helper text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Duration | `duration` | Text | No |  |  |

No results.

### Example

Wait 2 minutes after a deploy, so the service is up before a smoke test runs.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Task name** | `wait-for-start` |
| **Duration** | `120000`, which is 2 minutes in milliseconds |

The task shows **Waiting**, then **Succeeded** within about a second of its due time. The wait doesn't count towards the run's timeout. **Duration** can be a reference, such as `$(params.delay-ms)`. The task returns no results.

### Common problems

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The sleep ends almost at once | **Duration** is in milliseconds, so `120` waits 120 milliseconds. | Multiply seconds by 1,000: `120000` is 2 minutes. |
| The task stays **Running** instead of **Waiting**, and never ends | **Duration** isn't a whole number: it's blank, has a unit such as `2m`, or is a reference that resolved to text. | Cancel the run. Enter digits only, then save a new version. |
